v1_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-03). The majority (59%, E-02) of disputed bills were built from ACTUAL meter reads rather than estimates, and no tariff change occurred (E-04), so the surge is driven primarily by a billing-side defect in processing/validating accepted actual reads downstream of read collection - not by field-read/estimation shortfalls, which affect only a minority (41%, E-02) of disputes despite a real route-completion shortfall (0.88 vs 0.95 target, E-01) - and not by slow dispute response, which remains within SLA (E-05).
v2_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-03). For the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (41% of 3025 total, E-02), the dominant confirmed mechanism is billing-import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-13) coincident with the surge onset, which compares raw AMI register values against 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling; this causes legitimate reads from firmware v4.2 meters (register unit 0.1 m3, E-14) to be rejected REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION on import (1184/1240 such bills, E-12), forcing estimate substitution that drives disputes. The mechanism behind the majority 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (59%, E-02) is not yet established by evidence.
